description: Doubledecker on channel 1 plays a four-chord progression, C, A minor, F and G in C major, on steps 1, 5, 9 and 13 of every bar for four bars at 90 BPM, as triads at velocity 80 with Chd1 on the 3rd and Chd2 on the 5th, each chord two steps long. In the first two bars Harmony is Off, so the chords sound exactly as written, each in root position. In the last two bars Harmony Revoice is on. It keeps the same chords, with the same pitch classes, number of notes and rhythm, and only re-places the notes in other octaves, with each chord's root lowest. Listen for the same four chords being re-voiced at bar 3, about 5.3 seconds in, while the harmony stays the same.
synchronization: Observed framebuffer/grid sampled against host monotonic recording time; not sample-exact or physical-norns calibration.
title: Block chords, then Revoice
